accepted.finding: Below the already complete samekh foot are two upper lobes with a white window and an additional central lower node. The literal detached lamed segol has the same three-node triangular stamp; the same-font samekh qamats has a deep descending stem and the same-page bare final samekh lacks an added lower stamp. This surviving geometry certifies literal segol even though ink joins it to the foot.

The completed gimel body/foot has three additional rounded nodes below it: two upper stamps around a white window and a third central lower stamp. The detached same-font lamed segol anchors that triangular point class; the exact gimel tsere control retains only two low tips/window, while a detached qamats has a shoulder and deeper stem. The extra third stamp identifies segol without expected name spelling.

A broad shallow continuous lower bar extends rightward from the qof lower curve, with a long flat lower edge. Both exact same-font qof patah controls in הקרקע repeat this plateau. The qof tsere has two rounded low tips and a central valley, qamats has a deep center stem, and sheva has vertical stamps. The target preserves the flat bar discriminator despite its joins to the ordinary stem/curve.

Below the ordinary qof curve are two rounded low tips around a central valley/waist. The exact same-letter tsere in ומקל repeats the full two-node contour. Both qof patah controls instead have a long continuous plateau, qamats has an additional deep center stem, and sheva is vertical. No third central lower node survives here; the printed two-node arrangement supports tsere independently of expected verbal spelling.

The lamed descending oblique foot has an added horizontal two-node base, with two low tips and a middle valley/notch beyond the ordinary terminal. The detached same-verse lamed tsere repeats that pair. Same-page bare lamed controls end in a single oblique/rounded terminal; sheva has vertical nodes, segol a third central lower node, and detached exact-lamed qamats a crossbar with a deep stem. These controls resolve the bare-foot challenge and support tsere from surviving shape alone.
